+"""Lexical classification of manifest locations.
+
+Unlike :meth:`Code.path`, this performs no filesystem access: the location
+is classified purely by its textual form.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+
+def manifest_origin_label(value: object) -> str:
+    """Classify a manifest location as ``remote``, ``absolute``, ``relative`` or ``invalid``.
+
+    Returns ``remote`` when the text starts with ``http://`` or ``https://``,
+    ``absolute`` when it is a POSIX-rooted path, ``relative`` otherwise.
+    Returns ``invalid`` if converting *value* to text raises.
+    """
+    try:
+        text = str(value)
+    except Exception:
+        return "invalid"
+    if text.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
+        return "remote"
+    if text.startswith("/"):
+        return "absolute"
+    return "relative"
diff --git a/testing/test_manifest_origin_label.py b/testing/test_manifest_origin_label.py

+++ b/testing/test_manifest_origin_label.py
@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import pytest
+
+from _pytest.manifest_origin_label import manifest_origin_label
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("value", "expected"),
+    [
+        ("http://example.com/dist.toml", "remote"),
+        ("https://example.com/dist.toml", "remote"),
+        ("/srv/manifests/build.toml", "absolute"),
+        ("manifests/build.toml", "relative"),
+        ("build.toml", "relative"),
+        ("./build.toml", "relative"),
+        ("", "relative"),
+        (123, "relative"),
+        (None, "relative"),
+        ("/", "absolute"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_manifest_origin_label(value: object, expected: str) -> None:
+    assert manifest_origin_label(value) == expected
+
+
+def test_manifest_origin_label_invalid() -> None:
+    class Bad:
+        def __str__(self) -> str:
+            raise ValueError("nope")
+
+    assert manifest_origin_label(Bad()) == "invalid"
